title: optimize-autotune-orchestration-fallback-and-configuration-synchronization-playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: After Optimize auto-tuning rollout on 2026-03-08, multiple customer-facing routes experienced elevated latency and error rates for ~18 minutes. Root causes were a race during distributed config propagation and an aggressive batching profile applied without stage-specific traffic shaping. This ticket consolidates the incident follow-ups, documents mitigations, and creates an operational playbook for future autotune rollouts to ensure safe config synchronization, predictable fallbacks, and reversible applies.

Why this is high priority: autotune runs are system-level changes that affect per-token cost and latency SLOs. We need a robust, low-risk apply/rollback process and clear runbook for on-call to avoid regressions in production.

Scope: orchestration-level protections (leader-coordinated apply), preflight validation (dry-run and traffic shadowing), enhanced telemetry and rollback triggers, UI/UX changes to Optimize for visibility, and an on-call playbook with automated mitigations.
postmortem_summary:
During the March incident, two independent failures aligned: (1) optimize-agent nodes accepted a new batching config before all serving nodes had the compatible KV cache key-prefix update, producing a temporary cache miss storm and tail latency spikes; (2) the autoscaling controller interpreted the increased queue lengths as capacity demand and spun EC2/GPU nodes which increased cold-cache penalties and amplified the latency impact. The combination produced elevated 95/99th percentile latencies and ~2% error rate increase. No data loss; primary impact was customer-facing latency and increased token cost due to retries and amplification.

Contributing factors: lack of an atomic config apply protocol, insufficient preflight shadowing of production traffic, missing canary weight ramp and hysteresis for batching parameter changes, inadequate metric-based rollback triggers tied to cache health signals, and Optimize UI lacked a clear dry-run/preview mode.
mitigations: Implement leader-coordinated two-phase apply for Optimize config changes (prepare -> commit) to prevent partial rollouts
Add a traffic-shadow dry-run mode that replays a sampled subset of live requests against candidate configs in staging and stores latency/cost deltas
Introduce canary weight ramp with health checks (cache-hit ratio, p95 latency, error rate) and a mandatory minimum canary period
Decouple batching and caching changes into separate deployable units to avoid cross-dependencies in a single apply
Add automated rollback triggers: sustained >20% p95 increase OR cache-hit-ratio drop >15% for 5 minutes => automatic rollback
Expose before/after simulation summaries in Optimize UI and persist config snapshots for instant rollback
Extend autoscaler safeguards to ignore short-lived queue spikes caused by cache cold starts during config rollouts
Add retention of previous config for at least 24 hours with immutable audit trail
playbook_steps: Initial detection: On-call SRE receives Grafana alert for p95 latency or errors for route X. Check Optimize change log for recent 'autotune' commits within last 30 minutes.
Immediate mitigation: If an autotune change is detected, set CanaryWeight=0 via CLI flag to halt rollout. If Canary is already >0, apply emergency rollback to last snapshot through Optimize API.
Verification: Run quick health checks: cache_hit_ratio_by_prefix, p95 and p99 latency, request error classification. Post to incident channel with current metrics and link to dashboard.
If rollback fails or apply is inconsistent: trigger leader election for config-coordinator (manual in interim) and re-apply a prepared stable snapshot to all agent nodes.
Communication: Notify PM and stakeholders, open a postmortem ticket, and inform customers with SLO guardrails if risk threshold crossed.
Post-incident: Run traffic replay against candidate configs in staging and validate mitigations before next autotune run. Schedule an RCA doc and implementation tasks per action items.
acceptance_criteria: Config apply supports prepare/commit with atomic visibility: no serving node sees partial config
Optimize UI shows dry-run simulation report for each candidate config with cost/latency delta and a button to perform canary rollout
Automated rollback triggers are implemented and tested in staging (unit tests + e2e chaos job)
Decoupling of batching vs caching config is complete and documented
On-call playbook steps validated in drill and included in SRE runbook
action_items: ENG: Build config-coordinator microservice (owner: Daniel Kim) - ENG-20522
SRE: Add cache_hit_ratio and apply_latency panels to Optimize dashboard (owner: Maria Gonzales) - ENG-20523
FE: Add dry-run UI and canary controls to Optimize console (owner: Priya Shah) - PM ticket to follow
QA: Create replay-based validation harness for candidate configs (owner: Leo Nguyen) - include 95/99 latency checks
Infra: Implement autoscaler dampening policy changes to avoid reacting to short-lived cache cold starts (owner: Kevin Liu)
Docs: Publish 'Autotune safe rollout' playbook in Confluence and link from Optimize UI (owner: Samira Rahman)
risk: If implemented incorrectly, leader-coordinated apply could introduce single-point-of-failure—design must include fallback path
Automated rollback aggressiveness could cause oscillation if hysteresis not tuned
Traffic-shadowing sampling must be representative or false negatives may allow regressions
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created after incident. Initial triage by SRE and Optimize engineering. Assigned to Daniel Kim.
2026-03-11: Briefed PM and infra; created prototype two-phase apply PR; started dashboard updates. Maria added cache panels.
2026-03-12: QA estimated replay harness scope. Decided to decouple batching and caching changes; created sub-tasks for FE and Infra.
2026-03-13: Canaries and auto-rollback thresholds drafted and reviewed by SRE and Runtime leads. Waiting on security review for coordinator service (low risk).
2026-03-14: Priority P0 confirmed. Action items assigned in ticket. Scheduling tabletop drill next week to validate playbook.
